verdict.rationale: Gmail's own filters can match incoming mail by sender, subject or size and automatically apply labels, and a community user describes routing mail into a separate folder this way. That lets a user sort mail into labeled streams such as team or newsletters. The evidence does not show a split-inbox view, automatic importance ranking, or priority-ordered triage, so the streams must be built by hand. missing for 10: documented split-inbox or tabbed stream view, automatic important/priority classification, built-in newsletter and calendar-invite categorization, triage in priority order rather than arrival order.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can split my inbox into focused streams — important, team, newsletters, calendar invites — so triage happens in priority order, not arrival order

citations.quote: When a message matches, filters automatically trigger actions such as adding or removing labels
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
After you search, you can use the results to set up a filter for these messages.
